raj_dev: Hey CS team — onboarding run for tenant 'skyline' is flapping. We get a 200 from our auth proxy, then the first request 401, then a burst of 429s across our worker pool. Tokens are short-lived (~25s). Anyone familiar with a token->throttle cascade?
sara_cs: sorry to hear that. Can you paste a tiny sanitized trace (token response + first few failures)? Also how many workers at warmup?
raj_dev: logs (sanitized):
```
POST /auth/token -> 200 {token: \"tk.xyz\", ttl: 25}
POST /v1/chat -> 401 {error: \"invalid_token\"}
POST /v1/chat -> 429 {error: \"rate_limit\"} x 10
POST /v1/embeds -> 429
```
We spawn 45 worker processes at once during canary.
ben_infra: two likely causes: 1) short TTL + clock skew or token rounding (server sees token as already near-expiry); 2) refresh fanout — 45 first-requests in the same second trip our ephemeral burst protection. 401s are usually TTL/validation or duplicate-token revocation logic.
raj_dev: we mint per-process at start, not centralized.
sdk-ux: quick client-side fixes you can try now: 1) adopt tokenGraceMs (treat token as expiring ~5-8s earlier), 2) coalesce refreshes with a singleflight so multiple workers share the same refresh result for a short window, 3) cap init concurrency during warmup. Example:```js
client.setup({ tokenGraceMs:8000, maxInitConcurrent:6, refreshCoalesceMs:200 });
```
sara_cs: we can also temporarily raise your burst allowance for the canary while you apply fixes. Want +4rps for 24h?
raj_dev: yes please. Also any jitter pattern suggestions?
ben_infra: add randomized startup jitter per worker (0-400ms) and use a steady ramp (2-4 workers/sec) instead of an all-at-once spawn. If you must spawn many, centralize token issuance: one coordinator fetches N tokens and hands them out. That avoids the 1s fanout.
raj_dev: curious — if we centralize, is there any server-side risk with many workers reusing the same token?
ben_infra: reusing the same token across many clients can trigger duplicate-detection in some edge flows. Better to centralize the refresh but distribute delegated short-lived tokens per-worker when possible (delegate/exchange endpoint). If delegation isn't available, singleflight for refresh + short token-grace is a good compromise.
quota-bot: @sara_cs increased tenant "skyline" burst quota by +4 rps for 24 hours (chg: Z-44210).
raj_dev: implemented singleflight + reduced init concurrency to 5, added 200ms jitter. After ~10 minutes 401s vanished and 429s dropped to near zero. Thanks!
sara_cs: great — want me to add these steps to your onboarding playbook under "short-TTL auth patterns" so renewals & enablement see it?
raj_dev: yes, please capture: tokenGraceMs, singleflight, jitter, and an ops note that the auth proxy issues 25s TTL tokens. We'll follow up with a short doc on our token issuance cadence.
sdk-ux: follow-up: we'll add a short SDK snippet to docs recommending token coalescing and warmup pacing for TTL < 1min. Also opening a ticket to detect token-rotation + connection-reuse on the server and emit an `x-auth-stale` hint header to help debugging.
ben_infra: infra follow-up: consider a server-side metric that correlates first-request 401s + same-tenant fanout rate so we can auto-surface tenants likely hitting this. Filing INFRA-2147.
sara_cs: thanks all. Raj, good luck with the prod flip tomorrow — ping us if anything reappears.
raj_dev: will do, appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
